page: Amazon Web Services c6a.32xlarge is a high-density, compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It is powered by 64 physical cores and 128 vCPUs from an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor operating at clock speeds up to 3.6 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The server incorporates 256 GB of DDR4-3000 system memory, establishing a 2 GB per vCPU compute ratio. Network infrastructure provides a 50 Gbps baseline bandwidth. The configuration includes zero local storage, requiring external block storage for filesystem access, and contains no discrete GPU hardware accelerators.

Benchmark evaluations position this instance in the top 10% of tested systems for multi-threaded compute, verified by a stress-ng multi-core score of 190,692.91 and a PassMark CPU score of 98,563.74. Parallel compilation under Clang reached 58,030.0, and ray-tracing performance scored 113,760.0. The memory subsystem sustains 9,049.24 GB/sec in small cached reads and over 250 GB/sec for uncached blocks, supporting in-memory workloads like Redis at 137.19 million SET operations per second. In contrast, single-threaded performance is moderate, showing a Geekbench single-core score of 1,673.0.

Architectural tradeoffs center around execution model and storage structure. The AMD Zen 3 architecture supports AVX, AES-NI, and SHA extensions, but lacks AVX-512 and AMX instructions, limiting performance in advanced vector operations and large-model machine learning inference. Furthermore, without integrated NVMe drives, all disk I/O depends entirely on network storage channels, utilizing portions of the 50 Gbps fabric.

The c6a.32xlarge is suited for multi-threaded, parallel processing applications that do not depend on specialized matrix coprocessors. Common workload fits include distributed software compilation, batch processing, static web serving (tested at 55.53 GB/sec throughput), and in-memory caching clusters that benefit from dense core allocation and high network bandwidth.
description: Amazon Web Services c6a.32xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by a 64-core, 128-vCPU AMD EPYC 7R13 processor running at 3.6 GHz on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. Configured with 256 GB of DDR4-3000 memory, it offers a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio alongside a 50 Gbps baseline network interface. It lacks bundled local storage and discrete GPUs. Benchmark results establish top-tier multi-threaded processing capability, achieving high scores in stress-ng multi-core, PassMark CPU tests, and software compilation, complemented by 137.19 million Redis SET operations per second. While single-thread metrics and extended vector support like AVX-512 are limited, its 128 execution threads provide substantial multi-core density. The instance is structured for distributed compilation pipelines, large-scale batch computation, high-throughput static web hosting, and parallel data processing workloads reliant on dense x86_64 CPU resources and fast network throughput.
